message.content: In the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries, Europe was reshaped by the Reformation, royal centralization, and expanding trade. The Holy Roman Empire remained fragmented, while Poland’s elective monarchy offered Copernicus a relatively stable clerical and scholarly refuge. Political rivalries among papal states, monarchs, and Protestant reformers created an atmosphere where new astronomical ideas could circulate, yet also faced censorship and suspicion. Although his model was not cactiform, its heliocentric arrangement challenged medieval cosmology and reflected a broader crisis of authority.
